prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a rear-end collision. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1175; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant responds to Plaintiff's Original Petition as follows.

General Denial. Pursuant to Rule 92 of the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure, Defendant generally denies each and every allegation contained in Plaintiff's Original Petition and demands strict proof thereof by a preponderance of the evidence.

Affirmative Defenses. Without assuming any burden of proof that it would not otherwise bear, Defendant asserts the following defenses.

First, Plaintiff's own negligence caused or contributed to the collision. Plaintiff failed to keep a proper lookout, failed to control speed, and failed to maintain a safe following distance. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced by Plaintiff's percentage of responsibility, and Plaintiff may recover nothing if that percentage exceeds fifty percent.

Second, the collision and any claimed injuries were caused in whole or in part by the acts or omissions of a third party or persons over whom Defendant had no control, and Defendant requests that the responsible parties be designated under Section 33.004.

Third, Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by not following reasonable medical advice and by delaying necessary treatment. Any recovery must be reduced accordingly.

Defendant reserves the right to amend this answer as discovery proceeds.
